Customer: Small brand operator: founder-operator of a D2C brand with 100–2,000 orders a month and no finance team (assumption to test)
Problem and trigger: Month-end: net sales grew but cash did not, and nobody can say which orders or which return, discount or shipping policy lost money. Refunds, recovered stock, payment fees and handling are not tracked per order.
Current alternative: A spreadsheet of net sales checked weekly and profit checked monthly after the fact; gateway and marketplace payout reports read separately (assumption to test in interviews)
Value hypothesis: A monthly contribution report that nets refunds and recovered stock once, reconciles orders to channel and product totals, names the orders that lose money and saves one measurable intervention lets the founder act before the next month-end (assumption to test)
Price and unit: ₹1,500 per brand per month, monthly contribution-report subscription (price hypothesis; assumption to test)
Variable cost and unit: ₹280 per monthly report: analyst mapping and review ₹200, hosting share ₹50, payment collection ₹30 (assumption to test)
Contribution formula: Order level: net sales − (product cost − recovered cost) − shipping − payment fee − return cost − handling − ads; fixture (synthetic): ₹420 per kept order, −₹180 per returned order, ₹300 blended at a 20% return rate. Subscription level: price − cost to serve per report = ₹1,500 − ₹280 = ₹1,220 per brand per month (assumption to test)
Biggest unknown: Whether founders will share order-level refund and recovery data every month and pay for a report that shadows their own spreadsheet
Negotiated product change: Add refund and recovery semantics before a profit headline: contribution % is hidden until refund and recovery facts are complete (headline gate; API field totals.headline_ready)
Owner: M3 (Track 3) until MBA entry; then the MBA team lead [to fill]
Expected test: Sample order audit with 5 founders: at least 3 confirm a negative-contribution cause they did not track (threshold is an assumption)
First customer experiment: Sample order audit: map one month of a founder's order export to the C21 schema, walk through the ledger, leaks and one recommendation in a 30-minute call, then ask for a paid pilot of the monthly report at the hypothesis price
Stop rule: Stop the subscription test if fewer than 4 of 10 interviewed founders describe a profit-leak problem they want solved, or if none of 5 audited founders accepts a paid pilot at ₹999 a month or more
